review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no @[simp] lemmas of its own, so I judged the simp interface by the places where it falls back on manual rewriting. I checked the definitions of ideleNorm, cpowChar and etaFst/etaSnd in Definitions/. I searched Mathlib for conj/cpow lemmas and for an exp/cpow lemma. I searched the repository for other copies of the α-to-ideleNorm bridge. I did not run Lean, so every proposal is untested. The proposed bridge lemma would need care: it is stated only for the concrete α (or under hαdef), and the lemma would have to be orientation-safe. The conj-of-cpow suggestion is weaker, because it has a positivity side condition that simp may not discharge on its own. I did not report ofReal_exp_cpow, the indicator by_cases blocks, or measurable_ideleNorm, because no concrete simp-interface defect was evident.

findings.excerpt: have hnorm : ∀ x : (AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F)ˣ, ((α x : ℝˣ) : ℝ) = ideleNorm F x := by
findings.problem: The bridge ((α x : ℝˣ) : ℝ) = ideleNorm F x for α = toHomUnits (toRealHom ∘ distribHaarChar) is not a named simp lemma. The file re-proves it as a local hypothesis three times, at lines 79, 258 and 561 (by `rw [hαdef]; rfl` or `rfl`). Each time it re-derives hpos, the positivity of ideleNorm, by `▸`, although ideleNorm_pos already exists. The local hnorm is then threaded manually into `simp only [..., hnorm, ...]` and `rw [map_mul, ← hnorm, ...]`. The same `∀ x, ((α x : ℝˣ) : ℝ) = ideleNorm F x` hypothesis is also re-proved by `rfl` in several other files. So simp has no canonical normal form for the coercion of the concrete αm. Users must re-establish it by hand, and they must pass the αm unfolding hypothesis hαdef around.
findings.proposed_change: Add one shared lemma next to the definition of ideleNorm (or the eta family), stated for the concrete homomorphism. For example, `@[simp] theorem coe_toHomUnits_distribHaarChar_eq_ideleNorm (x) : (((NNReal.toRealHom : ℝ≥0 →+* ℝ).toMonoidHom.comp (distribHaarChar (AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F))).toHomUnits x : ℝˣ) : ℝ) = ideleNorm F x := rfl`. The orientation is α-coercion → ideleNorm F x, which is the normal form used throughout (ideleNorm_mul, ideleNorm_pos, ideleNorm_det_globalPoints). It cannot loop, because ideleNorm is not unfolded back. Then replace the local hnorm and hpos with this lemma and `ideleNorm_pos`. The `simp only [... hnorm ...]` calls become `simp only [..., this_lemma]` or plain `simp`, and the `hαdef` argument could disappear from eta_product_conj_eq₂, torus_window_integral_eq, torus_halfline_lo and torus_halfline_hi.
findings.benefit: Every user of the concrete αm gets the ideleNorm form automatically. The three copies of the same local hypothesis, and the repeated `hαdef` plumbing, go away. The theorems depend on the concrete definition instead of an opaque α with a definitional-equality hypothesis.

have hαN : ∀ x, ((α x : ℝˣ) : ℝ) = ideleNorm F x := fun x => rfl

findings.excerpt: rw [hconj _ (hpos z), hconj _ (hpos t), hconj _ (hpos z)]
findings.problem: The proof needs conj ((r:ℂ)^w) = (r:ℂ)^(conj w) for positive real r. It proves this as a local `hconj` through `Complex.cpow_conj` and an arg computation. It then applies it with three separate `rw`s, one of which repeats `hconj _ (hpos z)` because `rw` rewrites only one instantiation per call. Mathlib has only the hypothesis `x.arg ≠ π` versions (conj_cpow, cpow_conj, conj_cpow_eq_ite). So there is no simp-usable form for real bases, and the rewriting is done manually and order-sensitively.
findings.proposed_change: Extract `hconj` into a named top-level lemma, e.g. `conj_ofReal_cpow (hr : 0 ≤ r) (w : ℂ) : conj ((r:ℂ)^w) = (r:ℂ)^(conj w)`. The orientation pushes conj inward, which is safe because conj is not reintroduced. Use it as `simp only [conj_ofReal_cpow (hpos z).le, conj_ofReal_cpow (hpos t).le]`, or tag it @[simp] only if the 0 ≤ r side condition is dischargeable. This replaces the repeated `rw [hconj _ ...]` calls with a single `simp only` that rewrites all occurrences.
findings.benefit: The conjugation of cpow terms normalises in one `simp only`. It does not depend on rewrite order or on repeating the same instance. The lemma is also reusable in the other Maass–Selberg computations that use conj of cpow with real bases.

evidence.excerpt: theorem conj_cpow (x : ℂ) (n : ℂ) (hx : x.arg ≠ π) : conj x ^ n = conj (x ^ conj n)
